claims.text: Dissolving intergranular nanoprecipitates in tungsten-based plasma-facing materials increases high-temperature plastic strain.
Dissolving intergranular nanoprecipitates in tungsten-based plasma-facing materials increases high-temperature toughness.
The increase in plastic strain and toughness is caused by enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dislocation climb.
The initial tungsten-based alloy contains stable intergranular nanoprecipitates formed during fabrication.
The intergranular nanoprecipitates obstruct grain-boundary mobility.
A controlled thermal treatment can dissolve or reduce the precipitate phase without altering bulk composition.
Intergranular nanoprecipitates in the untreated material limit grain-boundary sliding.
Intergranular nanoprecipitates in the untreated material limit dislocation climb.
Dissolution of the precipitates removes obstacles to thermally activated plastic deformation.
Relative to the untreated baseline, treated material will exhibit higher plastic strain under identical high-temperature test conditions.
Relative to the untreated baseline, treated material will exhibit higher toughness under identical high-temperature test conditions.
The treated material will exhibit higher strain-rate sensitivity.
The treated material will exhibit improved resistance to crack propagation.
The proposed mechanism is relevant above approximately 1200 degrees Celsius in an inert or controlled atmosphere.
The proposed mechanism may not govern deformation under oxidizing conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not hold at temperatures where other deformation mechanisms dominate.
Treated and untreated specimens will be subjected to identical high-temperature tensile or creep tests to isolate the effect of the treatment.
Transmission electron microscopy can be used to verify reduction or absence of the intergranular nanoprecipitates after treatment.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in plastic strain and toughness relative to the untreated baseline is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to confirm precipitate reduction is designated as a falsifying outcome.
